newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble edges up on new reserve rule, o/n rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Rouble edges up on new reserve rule, o/n rates fall.

text.p: The rouble edged up on Monday as banks prepared for forthcoming higher dollar reserve rules but dealers said overnight credits fell as banks awaited higher rouble demand ahead of Treasury bill auctions.

Konversbank dealer Stanislav Belov said commercial banks could be selling dollars to decrease their reserve payments to the central bank ahead of a rise to 5.0 percent from 2.5 percent as of November 1.
"In the meantime, overnight credit rates could be low as banks have already set aside funds for the T-bill auctions," Belov said.
On Wednesday, October 30, the central bank is auctioning 12 trillion roubles of six-month paper. Auctions usually boost rouble demand on Mondays and Tuesdays.

"Overnight rates could be low and the dollar is stable as banks are expecting the rouble to rise tomorrow ahead of the auctions. This is why nobody is investing in dollars," Moscow Business World bank dealer Nikolai Zolotaryov said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,451-54 per dollar compared with an early 5,452-55 and 5,454-55 late on Friday. Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,451-54 per dollar from Friday's late 5,453-55.
The central bank said it had set 5,437/5,457 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded one to five percent compared with an early 20-30 percent and Friday's late 5-10 percent.
